record.file_problem: The full paper text is present, but some plotted labels and numerical values are garbled in the extracted figures.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares standard and variational SAEs and measures feature organization and interpretability using SAE benchmarks and t-SNE, rather than reproducing the original toy-model experiments.
record.gate_note: The study reports feature-geometry visualizations, feature examples, counts of active features, and SAE Bench outcomes. Many plotted benchmark values are not reliably readable, so only the results explicitly described in the text are recorded. Hyperparameter-selection details and cited results are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs as a tool and compares its own variational SAE with a standard TopK SAE on Pythia-70M, reporting only benchmark performance, feature death and t-SNE dispersion of dictionary features. It does not test toy-model superposition geometry (V1), the capacity or alternative accounts of polysemanticity (V2, V3), or whether SAE features are the model's units (V5) or 1-D (V6). Its two hand-picked interpretable features are illustrations of the tool, not an aggregate test of V4. The t-SNE 'dispersion' concerns SAE latents, not overlap of the model's feature directions.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors explicitly reject their hypothesis that variational sampling improves feature organization or interpretability. They attribute degraded core metrics to KL-driven feature death (82% fewer living features). They say SCR/TPP independence gains likely reflect the reduced dictionary size, and conclude that variational methods are not a promising direction for SAEs.
record.recipe_differences: This study compares a variational TopK SAE with a standard TopK SAE on Pythia-70M activations; it does not reproduce the original toy-network method or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with TopK sparsity and ablation threshold; the t-SNE comparison is reported for TopK=256.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding a KL term to a TopK SAE killed most latents (1,227 vs 6,970 features with recorded activations). It also gave better SCR/TPP independence scores and slightly worse reconstruction on Pythia-70M layer 0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE architecture choices (variational KL regularization) trade dictionary utilization against ablation-based feature-independence metrics.

record.problems: The study uses one language model and one dataset. The t-SNE geometry is indirect, the feature examples are selected examples, and extracted benchmark plots have garbled numerical labels. The paper itself notes substantially fewer living vSAE features, which complicates interpreting its independence gains.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results were omitted. Exact benchmark values could not be assigned reliably from the garbled extracted figures and are represented only where the text explicitly describes the comparison.

untested.parts: All: no toy model, no near-orthogonality or overlap measure, no sparsity-dependent transition, no geometry.
All: no test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions.
No aggregate measure of features being spread across neurons or of SAE sparse-feature recovery. Only two selected example features are shown.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not tested. Feature death in the vSAE is an architecture issue only.

record.verdict_notes: This is an SAE-method paper that does not bear on the superposition claim versions. The record's 'tests/T2' and its labels for V1 and V4 are unsupported and should be dropped. Internal inconsistencies: Methods says 2,048 features, but subject names say d8192 and the histogram reports 6,970 SAE features. The Conclusion says reduced cosine similarity, while Section 4.1 says vSAE slightly outperforms on it. Section 4.2 says no large interpretability difference was found between the networks. Single model, single layer (layer 0), single dataset.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the original toy-network setup directly, near-orthogonality or overlap of feature directions, interference as a cost of superposition, a sparsity-dependent geometric transition, or dependence on feature importance.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity results from competition for dimensions or whether important features get dedicated dimensions while others share.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity alone is evidence of superposition.
Tests SAE feature recovery and interpretability on Pythia-70M, not whether real-model features are spread across many neurons.
Does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.
